c.tagline: First Ottoman capital, cradled by Mount Uludağ and steaming with silk and thermal springs.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered; the BiTaksi app and Uber both dispatch licensed metered taxis rather than private cars.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's unified emergency number connecting to ambulance, fire and police.

avoid.reason: Watch pockets in the crowded Grand Bazaar and Kapalicarsi lanes, and insist taxis run the meter.

hood_desc: Bursa's historic core around Ulu Cami (the Grand Mosque), the covered bazaar and the Koza Han silk khan, and Heykel square — the walkable heart where first-timers should base themselves for sights, shopping and İskender kebab.
The hillside thermal-spa quarter west of center, famous since Roman and Ottoman times for its hot springs; lined with spa hotels and quiet leafy streets, ideal for a relaxed soak-and-stay.
Bursa's modern western district of wide avenues, university campuses, shopping malls and contemporary restaurants and bars — the newer city center where dining and nightlife concentrate.
The eastern district holding the Green Mosque and Green Tomb (Yeşil Cami and Yeşil Türbe) and the Emir Sultan complex; a traditional, sight-rich quarter of early-Ottoman monuments.
A 700-year-old UNESCO-listed Ottoman village on the lower slopes of Mount Uludağ, about 10 km east, with cobbled lanes and painted timber houses; a tranquil escape known for its village breakfasts.
lodging: Almira Hotel Thermal Spa & Convention Center

water.note: Locals often drink the mountain-fed tap water, but most visitors stick to bottled.

transit.hours: Bursaray and city buses run roughly 6:00 AM to midnight; there is no dedicated night service, so taxis or ride apps cover late hours.
transit.note: Bursa's backbone is the Bursaray light-metro line crossing the city east-west, complemented by tram lines and the extensive BURULAŞ city bus network.
transit.pay: Travel is paid with the rechargeable BuKart smart card tapped on entry; single fares are low and transfers between metro, tram and bus are discounted. Contactless bank cards work on many lines.

bus: Intercity coaches from Bursa Terminal (Otogar) to Istanbul, Ankara and İzmir
ferry: BUDO / İDO fast ferries across the Sea of Marmara between Mudanya/Güzelyalı and Istanbul
train: Bursaray light rail (no mainline intercity rail station in the city)

transit.m: Municipal bus toward Yenişehir/city (limited daytime service, ~75 min)
Note: many travelers instead fly into Istanbul and take the BUDO/İDO fast ferry across the Sea of Marmara to Mudanya, then a short bus into Bursa.

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Iskender kebap
food.desc: Bursa's own invention: shaved doner over cubed pide, doused in tomato sauce and sizzling butter with a spoonful of thick yogurt.

places.name: Kebapci Iskender
places.note: Run by the inventor's family; one dish only, finished tableside with melted butter.

places.name: Iskender 1867
places.note: Ornate Ottoman-style room from the same lineage, garden views and antique decor.

places.name: Adanur Hacibey
places.note: Long-running rival house locals rate for its lighter tomato sauce and crisp pide base.

food.name: Inegol kofte
food.desc: Flat, juicy grilled meatballs of beef and lamb bound with onion and breadcrumb, no spice bomb; from the town of Inegol east of Bursa.

places.name: Cumhuriyet Koftecisi
places.note: Long-established koftehane on Inegol's main street, charcoal-grilled to order.

places.name: Inegol koftecis of Cumhuriyet Caddesi
places.note: A whole strip of grill houses within 40 minutes of Bursa; pick the busiest at lunch.

places.name: Heykel kofte salons
places.note: Central Bursa branches serve the Inegol style if you are not making the day trip.

food.name: Cantik
food.desc: Small, thick Bursa flatbread topped with spiced minced meat, baked in a stone oven and eaten by the handful with ayran.

places.name: Bakeries of the Kapalicarsi
places.note: Bazaar-lane ovens sell cantik hot from mid-morning; cheapest and most authentic.

places.name: Tahtakale food street
places.note: Row of pide and cantik ovens near the bazaar, busy with market traders.

places.name: Heykel pide houses
places.note: Central pidecis list cantik alongside tahinli pide; easy to combine with sightseeing.

food.name: Pideli kofte
food.desc: Grilled kofte laid on buttery pide squares with tomato sauce and yogurt; the everyday Bursa cousin of Iskender.

places.name: Heykel pideli kofte salons
places.note: Cluster of old-school lunch counters around the Ataturk statue; fast and cheap.

places.name: Kapalicarsi lokantas
places.note: Bazaar tradesmen's canteens plate it at midday; look for the queue of locals.

places.name: Tahtakale food street
places.note: Grill houses here do the buttered-pide version well, often with house-churned ayran.

food.name: Kemalpasa tatlisi
food.desc: Small cheese-dough spheres fried then soaked in sugar syrup, served warm with clotted cream; from nearby Mustafakemalpasa.

places.name: Kemalpasa tatlicilari
places.note: Dedicated dessert shops serve it warm in syrup with kaymak; ask for it hot.

places.name: Mustafakemalpasa town centre
places.note: The source town, about an hour west; dozens of shops make it fresh all day.

places.name: Koza Han dessert stalls
places.note: Silk-market courtyard shops pair it with tea in a 15th-century han.

food.name: Kestane sekeri
food.desc: Candied chestnuts from the forests of Mount Uludag, slowly glazed in syrup; Bursa's most famous sweet souvenir.

places.name: Kafkas
places.note: The best-known kestane sekeri house in Bursa; also does chestnut chocolates.

places.name: Koza Han shops
places.note: Historic silk-han courtyard lined with confectioners selling boxed chestnuts.

places.name: Kulturpark-area confectioners
places.note: Branches near the park for gift boxes, with samples before you buy.

food.name: Ayran
food.desc: Salted yogurt drink, often churned to a foam head in Bursa and considered the only correct partner for Iskender.

places.name: Kebapci Iskender
places.note: Serves the frothy churned style in metal cups alongside its single dish.

places.name: Adanur Hacibey
places.note: House ayran poured from the churn; ask for the foamy top.

places.name: Tahtakale food street
places.note: Street stalls sell cold churned ayran by the glass for pocket change.

food.name: Turkish tea and coffee
food.desc: Tulip glasses of black tea and thick Turkish coffee, taken slowly in Bursa's Ottoman han courtyards.

places.name: Koza Han courtyard
places.note: Tea garden under mulberry trees in the 1491 silk han; the classic Bursa pause.

places.name: Umurbey / Setbasi cay bahcesi
places.note: Terrace tea gardens with valley views above the Gok Dere gorge.

places.name: Uludag summit cafes
places.note: Cable-car-top cafes serve tea with mountain views over the whole plain.

landmarks: Ulu Cami (Grand Mosque)
Bursa's monumental Seljuk-style mosque of 1399 shelters twenty domes, a serene indoor fountain, and some of the finest Islamic calligraphy panels in all of Türkiye.
Yeşil Türbe (Green Tomb)
Sheathed in luminous turquoise tiles, this hexagonal mausoleum of Sultan Mehmed I crowns a cypress-shaded hill and reigns as the city's most beloved emblem.
Yeşil Cami (Green Mosque)
A masterpiece of early Ottoman architecture from 1421, its interior dazzles with intricate İznik tilework, carved marble portals, and a jewel-box royal loge.
Koza Han (Silk Cocoon Caravanserai)
Silk traders have haggled in this elegant 1491 courtyard caravanserai for five centuries; today its plane-shaded tea gardens and scarf shops enchant every visitor.
Cumalıkızık Village
A UNESCO-listed 700-year-old Ottoman village on Uludağ's slopes, where crooked cobbled lanes wind past pastel timber-framed houses and grandmothers sell homemade jams.
Uludağ (Mount Olympus of Mysia)
Türkiye's premier ski mountain looms 2,543 meters above Bursa, reached by one of the world's longest cable cars for alpine meadows and sweeping panoramas.
Muradiye Complex
Twelve exquisitely tiled royal tombs, including that of tragic prince Cem Sultan, cluster in rose gardens around Sultan Murad II's tranquil 15th-century mosque.
Bursa Grand Bazaar (Kapalı Çarşı)
A labyrinth of covered arcades and historic hans where locals shop for silk, towels, and knife-made İskender kebab, far less touristy than Istanbul's version.
Tophane Clock Tower and Park
Perched on the citadel where the Ottoman Empire was born, this slender 1905 clock tower overlooks the tombs of founders Osman and Orhan Gazi.
Irgandı Bridge
One of the world's few surviving bazaar bridges, this restored 1442 Ottoman span across the Gökdere stream is lined with artisan workshops and cafes.

train.note: Bursa has no working intercity passenger railway. The old Mudanya line closed decades ago and the planned Bursa-Bilecik high-speed link to the YHT network is still under construction, so the city has only its own metro. The nearest mainline station is at Bilecik or Eskişehir, both about two hours away by road.

bus.note: No international coaches. Bursa's Terminal north of the centre is well served: Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/) and Metro Turizm (https://www.metroturizm.com.tr/en) run constantly to Istanbul (about 2h30 including the Osmangazi bridge), Ankara, İzmir and the Aegean coast. Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/). Many Istanbul services combine a coach with the Marmara ferry.

intl.to: Istanbul - Yenikapı & Kadıköy (Türkiye) - fast catamaran from Mudanya or Güzelyalı, ~2 hr door to door

ferry.note: There are no international sailings, but the Sea of Marmara fast ferries are the smart way to and from Istanbul, cutting out the long drive around the bay. Boats leave from Mudanya and Güzelyalı, roughly 30 minutes from central Bursa by shuttle or taxi, and İDO also carries cars. Sailings are reduced in winter and can be cancelled in rough weather.

half.name: İznik
half.blurb: Ancient Nicaea on a lake shore, famed for its Ottoman-era ceramic tiles and Byzantine city walls.

half.name: Gemlik
half.blurb: Coastal town on the Sea of Marmara known for its olive groves, olive-oil production and quiet waterfront promenade.

full.name: Istanbul
full.blurb: Turkey's largest city, reached by ferry across the Sea of Marmara, with the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque and Grand Bazaar.
